newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia govt says plans to close London Club Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: Russia govt says plans to close London Club Aug 15.

text.p: Russia plans to close an agreement with the London Club of commercial bank creditors by August 15, 1997, a joint statement by the government and the central bank said on Thursday.

"The government of the Russian Federation plans to close the 1996 agreement with commercial banks-creditors on debt restructuring by August 15, 1997," the statement, published in the Central Bank of Russia's official magazine, said.
In 1995 Russia agreed with the London Club to reschedule $35 billion in debts inherited from the Soviet Union and interest arrears for up to 25 years.
To close the agreement, Russia must reconcile a minimum of $20 billion of the debt. A senior Finance Ministry official said earlier Russia hoped to reconcile the sum by mid-July.
The statement said Russia hoped to close agreements with national clubs of creditors by the end of June 1997 and to start issuing promissory notes.
It also said the government was firm in its intentions to stick to a repayment schedule.
